subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric is a young human guard with a bowl-cut, assigned to crowd control at the tower entrance; he admitted his role was not observational and felt embarrassment upon realizing his job was insufficient for the scale of the event; he confirmed the timeline of arrivals and departures around the death of Janussi.
source_quote: I was told to make sure only the right people came in and out.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan was the previous guard at the tower door, relieved before the party’s arrival; Tadric noted he looked more determined leaving than entering, suggesting he had encountered something significant before being removed from duty.
source_quote: Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was found dead by the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore and housekeeper Miss Hollypocket around 7:30 a.m.; the cause and circumstances of death remain unexamined by the party, though a death rite was already performed by the Gate Warden.
source_quote: Janussi found dead by the Great Reader and the housekeeper, one Miss Hollypocket, around half past seven in the morning.

subject: Gate Warden
fact: The Gate Warden arrived at 8 a.m., spoke briefly with the discoverers, returned alone at 11 a.m. for a full inspection, and exited with an expression of discovery; he was removed from duty before being questioned, and his findings remain undisclosed.
source_quote: The Gate Warden again at eleven, alone, for a full inspection — careful, deliberate, left to make his report to the Council.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani arrived shortly after 8 a.m., distraught, and was permitted only a doorway view of the body; no further interaction occurred.
source_quote: Kazryn Nyantani, distraught, shortly after eight — allowed to see the body but only from the doorway.

subject: Fheminor Scrivenbark
fact: Fheminor Scrivenbark arrived at 8:30 a.m., appeared shocked, and requested to inspect the chamber but was turned away.
source_quote: Fheminor Scrivenbark at half past eight, appearing shocked, wanting to inspect the chamber, turned away.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm arrived at 9 a.m. from the baths and was granted a brief look at the body before confirming the existing orders; she later provided theological commentary on the cat.
source_quote: Bookwyrm at nine, arriving from the baths, allowed a brief look before confirming the existing orders.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is a dwarf who became increasingly agitated after the second landing; he insists the cat is not a supernatural entity but a normal cat, despite evidence suggesting otherwise; he later revised his definition of 'anything' to include legal boundaries.
source_quote: These Avowed had taken a cat sitting wherever it liked and turned it into an interstellar, interspatial, interdimensional horror — that's just what cats do.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a drow who quietly questioned whether the cat might be something more than it appears; his single word — 'Is it?' — caused Fembris to reconsider his position.
source_quote: Is it?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dragonborn investigator who consistently focuses on structural truths: he identifies testimony as evidence, proposes examining people as objects of inquiry, and notes the fragility of the corpse due to elapsed time since death.
source_quote: But your testimony is evidence. Maybe you are evidence, and we should examine you.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is a half-orc who offered a theological disclaimer regarding the cat, asserting that no one has conclusively proven it is or is not a power that lives here; she later stepped around the cat without fear.
source_quote: Nobody had been able to conclusively prove the cat was some kind of power that lived here, and nobody had been able to conclusively prove that it was not.

subject: The Cat
fact: The cat is gray, with yellow eyes, motionless until approached, then tracks movement without needing to move itself; it has been observed multiple times by different individuals; its nature is debated as either mundane or supernatural; it has been described as a familiar, shapeshifter, or interdimensional entity, though no proof exists either way.
source_quote: Gray. Motionless. Yellow eyes that opened the moment we got close. The cat had decided it need not move for anyone, and tracked us anyway.

subject: The Tower
fact: The tower contains a spiraling staircase with key locations on each landing: a reception chamber on the first, a shrine of Oghma on the second, and a large apartment with its door left conspicuously ajar on the third; the apartment has not yet been entered by the party.
source_quote: Reception chamber at the first landing, a shrine of Oghma at the second, a large apartment at the third with its door left conspicuously ajar.

subject: The Third-Floor Apartment
fact: The third-floor apartment’s door is left open, a deliberate anomaly in an otherwise controlled environment; it has been noted and filed for later examination, as it is the only unsecured interior space in the tower.
source_quote: I noted the apartment. Noted that the door was open. Filed it for later.

subject: The Death Rite
fact: A death rite has already been performed on Janussi’s corpse by the Gate Warden prior to the party’s arrival; this renders the rite unusable for another attempt for a significant duration, delaying any spiritual inquiry.
source_quote: Someone — presumably the Gate Warden, before his removal — had already used the rite on the corpse, which meant we'd be waiting if we wanted to try again.

subject: Removal of the Gate Warden
fact: The Gate Warden was removed from duty after conducting a full inspection of the crime scene and before being questioned; his removal suggests an attempt to suppress or control the flow of information regarding his findings.
source_quote: The Gate Warden removed before he could be asked what he'd found.

subject: The Open Door
fact: The open door of the third-floor apartment is an unexplained anomaly in a highly controlled environment; its purpose and contents are unknown, but its existence implies a deliberate act or hidden evidence.
source_quote: A door left ajar on the third floor landing.

subject: The Cat's Nature
fact: The cat’s behavior and the conflicting interpretations of it by the party suggest a hidden supernatural truth; its persistence, indifference, and the theological debate surrounding it imply it is more than it appears — or that someone wants others to believe it is.
source_quote: That's kind of how cats always are, I think," I said, because it is.

subject: The Gate Warden's Discovery
fact: The Gate Warden exited the crime scene after his inspection with a demeanor of discovery, yet was removed before reporting; his findings remain unknown, making him the most critical unspoken witness.
source_quote: Tadric noted that Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in.

subject: The Unobserved Gap
fact: Tadric admitted he was not observing, only controlling; the Gate Warden’s movements inside the chamber during his inspection were unrecorded; this gap in observation is the most significant vulnerability in the timeline.
source_quote: He had not been watching closely enough to track what he'd done in there.

subject: The Need to Enter
fact: The party has not yet entered the third-floor apartment; its open door, proximity to the crime scene, and lack of documentation make it the next logical point of inquiry — the place where answers may be hidden.
source_quote: I hadn't been inside yet. That was where I needed to be.
